name: backend-legacy
description: Hard backend tasks on the ts-backend-legacy fixture, where the difficulty is finding the cause in a big, messy codebase rather than following a long requirement list: symptom-only bug reports, invariants that imply concurrency and integer money, a tenant-isolation sweep, a measured performance budget, spec conformance and spec-sized changes across old and new code. Scored per hidden test case.

tasks.prompt:
Support ticket from Acme, can you take this one?

> Our developer Sam works from Sydney. On Monday morning (his time) he logged 2 hours, and the weekly timesheet shows them on Sunday, in the week before. Payroll goes off the same numbers, so this matters to us.

Time should always count on the calendar day it was logged on, for the person who logged it, wherever they are. Please fix this properly.

Finance wants to give customers part of their money back on invoices they've paid. Please add POST /api/invoices/:id/refunds for admins, taking {"amountCents": <whole number>, "reason": "<text>"} and answering 201 with the refund (id, invoiceId, amountCents, reason, createdAt). GET /api/invoices/:id should show refundedCents as well.

The money rules: a refund can never take back more than was actually paid on that invoice (all its refunds together), and the ledger must always balance: every refund shows up in GET /api/ledger as a negative "refund" entry, and the org's ledger balance never goes below zero. Refuse a refund that would break this with 409; invalid amounts are a 422.

Our finance tool will call this the same way it calls the payments endpoint, retries included.

A pen-test report came in: a user in one organization can read another organization's data through at least one endpoint of our API. They didn't say which ones. Find and fix every place where one org can read or change another org's data.

Another org's data has to behave as if it doesn't exist: 404 for anything addressed by id (directly or nested under something else), and nothing of it in lists, filters or exports. Normal access within an org must keep working.
